question: P-525 (P-510's pre-seal condition for THE FINAL ATTACK's Step B): is the L2 Gram matrix of the three matter zero modes of each field (Q, u, d, L, e), at the census lines' twists, proportional to the identity (T-NORM), for FR-FIB as the census evaluator computes it? Data-free: no measured Standard Model number was read or compared.
verdict_scope: Exactly, as a theorem, and the quadrature confirms it. Over 1170 configurations the invariant off-diagonals are <= 2.0e-12 at n = 32. On the worst classes (all at Im tau = 6) they fall to <= 1.0e-15 at n = 48 and <= 6e-16 at n = 64. The diagonal spread is exactly 0. For FR-FIB's matter zero modes the Gram matrix under ANY flat-invariant hermitian metric is G = H * ||F_x||^2. H is the metric's own 3x3 matrix in the intertwiner basis C_p C_q^-1. The modes contribute only the common scalar ||F_x||^2, at every tau, line and field. In the frame's metric (H = I: the 4-fold-cover / product typing the census uses), G = ||F_x||^2 * I_3 exactly: zero off-diagonals and equal diagonals. T-NORM is NOT forced by the flat bundles alone. The three generation bundles V_x (x) L_chi_p are mutually isomorphic, so the flat-invariant metrics form a family of real dimension 9 (computed). B1654 section 1.11's reason ('no invariant pairing joins sections of different flat bundles') is false as stated; its result ||F||^2 * I_3 is exact for H = I.
zero_modes: Read from the frame's code, frontier/B1691_the_exponents_at_the_two_fixed_points/verification/correction/b1656_funcs.py. Take a field of charge q (6Y: Q 1, u -4, d 2, L -3, e 6; b1656_funcs.py:22, cm_zero_line.py:38) on the line w = p1 tau - p2 (b1656_funcs.py:42). It has the twist (a, b) = twist_of(q w) = (q p1, -2 q p2) (b1656_funcs.py:41,43; cm_zero_line.py:58). Its zero mode is the doublet F_x(z) = ( th[a,b](z; 2tau)/sqrt th1(z; tau), e^{i pi b} th[a,b](z+tau; 2tau)/sqrt th1(z+tau; tau) ), with the branch of bil(): F0 F1 = X0 X1/(i e^{-i pi tau/2} e^{-i pi z} th1(z; tau)) (b1656_funcs.py:28-38). Untwisted, this is the SM seat's W21 mode F = (f(z), f(z+tau)), f = th3(z; 2tau)/sqrt th1(z; tau) (frontier/B1642_the_golden_coupling_as_the_zero_modes_residue/verification/residue_coupling.py:4-8). The three generations are psi_p = C_p F_x, with C_p in BLOCKS = [QJ, QI, QK] (b1656_funcs.py:21) and the SAME F_x for all three. The coupling reads Y_ab = (C_a F_x)^T eps S (C_b F_y) (coupling(), b1656_funcs.py:126), and cm_zero_line.py:73-74 takes its SVD. My independent theta code reproduces the frame's bil() to 1.8e-15 and its twists exactly (plumbing_against_the_frame). These are NOT magnetised-torus theta modes. F_x is a section of a FLAT (degree-0) rank-2 bundle V_x with a branch point at the puncture (|F_x|^2 ~ 1/|z|). Its monodromy is Phi(1) ~ QI and Phi(tau) ~ QJ, up to U(1) phases set by the line: r = F1/F0 obeys r(z+1) = -r(z) and r(z+tau) r(z) = -1 at every configuration. That is an irreducible Q8 representation. The generations differ only by the constant unit quaternions C_p. They carry three distinct non-trivial characters (chi(1), chi(tau)): j (-1, +1), i (+1, -1), k (-1, -1).
inner_product: The flat L2 product <psi, psi'> = int_E h(psi, psi') dA over a fundamental cell of the fibre torus E = C/(Z + tau Z), with dA = Im tau dx dt for z = x + t tau. On V_x the flat hermitian metric is unique up to scale (Schur: Phi(1), Phi(tau) generate an irreducible group), and it is the standard C^2 metric. There is no Gaussian e^{-pi k (Im z)^2/Im tau} factor. V_x has degree 0: the th[a,b](.; 2tau) numerator and the sqrt th1 denominator carry the same automorphy factor, so |F_x|^2 is doubly periodic (checked at every configuration). Across the three generations the metric has a 3x3 block matrix H (see theorem); the frame takes H = I. The puncture's 1/|z| is integrable. It is integrated by the Duffy corner map, with the cell split so that the puncture sits at a corner, and cross-checked by an independent polar quadrature about the puncture.

controls.positive: (i) The puncture quadrature: int_P dA/|z| over skewed cells (tau = i, 0.3+1.2i, 0.45+2.6i), Duffy against a 30-digit polar reference: relative error <= 7e-16, and exactly 4 ln(1+sqrt 2) at tau = i. (ii) The classical case: magnetised-torus modes th[j/N,0](Nz; N tau) with h = exp(-2 pi N (Im z)^2/Im tau), for N = 2, 3, 5 at tau = i, 0.3+1.2i, 0.5+2.5i, each on three different cells (centred at 0, lattice corners, generic). Every off-diagonal is <= 1.3e-15, and every diagonal equals the exact sqrt(Im tau/(2N)) to <= 1.1e-14. (iii) ||F_x||^2 of the frame's modes on the cell centred at the puncture, by Duffy and by polar quadrature: the two agree to <= 1.3e-14 at every one of the 306 twist classes.
controls.negative: (i) The magnetised basis psi_1 + 0.3 psi_0 (N = 3) must show its off-diagonal 0.3/sqrt(1.09) = 0.2873478855663454 and diagonal ratio 1.09. Found 0.28734788556634516 and 1.0900000000000007. (ii) The frame with its QI block rotated to cos(0.3) QI + sin(0.3) QJ must show the invariant (cover) off-diagonal (QJ, C') = sin 0.3 = 0.29552020666133955. Found 0.2955202066613397 at tau = i and at 0.35+2.75i. Its second entry (C', QK) must be 0, because both of its terms are cross terms with non-trivial characters. Found 2.3e-17 and 1.3e-16. Disclosed: tnorm.py first labelled that second prediction sin(theta), an error of mine; refine.py corrects the label after the run, and the measured values are unchanged. (iii) A flat-invariant NON-product metric H (off-diagonals 0.2 and 0.1i): the integrator returns G = H ||F||^2 on every cell, independent of the cell. This is a genuine kinetic mixing that the flat structure allows. (iv) The naive componentwise cross pairing int_cell (C_p F)^dagger (C_q F) is not an invariant, and the run shows it behaving as one would expect of a section of a non-trivial flat line bundle. It is large on single cells: up to 0.99985 on the cell centred at the puncture and up to 0.885 on the cell centred at (1+tau)/2, and the two cells differ by up to 1.57. It flips sign under period shifts by the cross character, with residual 0.0 at the stored 12 digits. Its invariant average over the 4-fold cover is 0 (results_summary).

theorem: (1) Unitarity: C_p is in SU(2), so |C_p F_x|^2 = |F_x|^2 pointwise. The three diagonal densities are one function, so the diagonals are equal on any cell. (2) Character orthogonality. This is the mechanism of the classical theorem that magnetised-torus theta functions with characteristics are orthonormal: eigenfunctions of a unitary translation group with distinct characters are orthogonal under an invariant metric. Here C_p F_x(z + gamma) = chi_p(gamma) Phi(gamma) C_p F_x(z), so (C_p F)^dagger (C_q F) is a section of the flat line bundle L_{chi_p chi_q}, which is non-trivial for p != q. On the 4-fold cover C/2Lambda, where every character is trivial, its integral is sum over gamma in Lambda/2Lambda of chi_p chi_q(gamma) * I = 0. (3) Schur. V_x is irreducible and V_x (x) L_chi is isomorphic to V_x via C_p, so Hom_flat(V_x (x) L_chi_q, V_x (x) L_chi_p) = C * C_p C_q^-1. Every flat-invariant hermitian metric on the three generations is therefore h = sum_pq H_pq psi_p^dagger C_p C_q^-1 psi'_q with H in Herm_3^+ (real dimension 9, computed). On the zero modes G = H * ||F_x||^2, because C_p^dagger C_p C_q^-1 C_q = 1. Hence T-NORM <=> H proportional to I: a property of the metric, never of the modes, tau or the line. Which typings force it, with the real dimension of the invariant metrics computed in each: (a) The flat bundles alone allow dimension 9, so they force nothing. (b) The characters imposed as a symmetry of the multiplicity index alone give dimension 3: H diagonal, but the norms may differ. (c) Any symmetry acting diagonally through SU(2) on V (x) M allows a democratic mixing b I + c J (2 (x) 3 = 2 + 4; checked: P_2 restricted to the modes is J/3). (d) H = I is forced (dimension 1) in the 4-fold-cover typing: the generations are the non-trivial deck-isotypic components of one field on C/2Lambda with a deck-invariant metric. (e) H = I is also forced by a product metric h_V (x) h_M whose M factor is invariant under a group acting irreducibly on M alone. B1654 section 1.11's sentence 'no invariant pairing joins sections of different flat bundles' is false as stated: C_p C_q^-1 is such a pairing (invariance residual 0.0). Its result ||F||^2 * I_3 is exact for H = I.
consequence_for_the_census: The running census does NOT need to be stopped. It takes the SVD of Y in the basis {C_p F_x}. In the frame's metric (H = I) that basis is exactly orthonormal at every tau and line, up to one scale per field (||F_x||^2, which differs between fields and lines). Every stored output (m1/m3, m2/m3, |V_us|, |V_cb|, |V_ub|, J) is invariant under that scale. So no census row is in a wrong kinetic frame relative to FR-FIB as typed. What this adds for Step B's seal: T-NORM's line on the frame card should read 'exact for FR-FIB's zero modes (P-525: G = H ||F_x||^2, the modes contribute a common scalar only); H = I is the frame's typing (4-fold cover / product), CHOSEN, not forced by the flat bundles (which allow H in Herm_3^+, 8 real parameters per field modulo scale)'. B1654 section 1.11's reason (and P-109/P-112/P-146's closing notes that quote it) needs a dated correction. If a ruling ever admitted H != I, that would be a different frame with new continuous data. The census as stored (outputs only, no Y) could not be re-weighted and would have to be recomputed. That is a frame change, not an error in the present run. A size bound for that case: with kinetic matrices K_L, K_R, every mass ratio m_i/m_3 moves by at most a factor sqrt(cond K_L * cond K_R), from sigma_i(A Y B) <= ||A|| sigma_i(Y) ||B|| and its inverse. For example, condition numbers 1.1 give at most 0.041 decades. The CKM entries have no such uniform bound.

method: One process with 3 workers, nice 10, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1. The theta series are my own (NK = 24, checked against NK = 60). Quadrature: Gauss-Legendre with n = 20 and 32. The Duffy corner map is used on quadrants with the puncture at a corner. The invariant Gram is (1/4) of the integral over the 4-fold cover's fundamental domain [-0.37113, 1.62887] x [-0.42371, 1.57629] in (x, t), a generic offset, so the nodes in different translates are not lattice translates. Single cells were also integrated: centred at the puncture, centred at (1+tau)/2, and shifted by 1 and by tau. A polar route about the puncture was used on the centred cell. Sample: tau in {i, 0.25+i, 0.5+1.5i, 0.05+2.05i, 0.35+2.75i, 0.2+3i, 0.85+3.45i, 0.5+4i, 0.3+6i}. Lines: the zero line; (2/5, k/10) for k = 0..9; order 4: (1/4,0), (0,1/4), (1/4,1/4), (1/4,1/2), (1/2,1/4), (1/4,3/4); order 2: (1/2,0), (0,1/2), (1/2,1/2); order 3: (1/3,0), (1/3,2/3); order 9: (1/9,1/9); order 12: (1/12,5/12), (5/12,1/12); order 7: (2/7,3/7). All five fields on every line, 1170 configurations in all. Every configuration was checked for its structure (monodromy, characters, periodicity). Configurations sharing a twist class (a mod 1, b mod 1, tau) have the same Gram up to constant phases, so the Gram was integrated once per class: 306 classes.
suggested_register_items: B1654 section 1.11's reason for T-NORM ('no invariant pairing joins sections of different flat bundles') is false: the generation bundles are isomorphic via C_p C_q^-1, and the flat-invariant metrics on one field's three generations have real dimension 9. Its result is exact for H = I. P-109, P-112 and P-146 close on that reason, so they need dated notes.

T-NORM's label on Step B's frame card: exact for FR-FIB's modes (G = H ||F_x||^2); H = I is FR-FIB's typing (CHOSEN unless derived). It is FORCED within the 4-fold-cover typing. The flat structure alone ADMITS H in Herm_3^+.

A possible derivation of the cover typing, not checked here: by Shapiro's lemma W10's space (+)_p H^1(F_2; chi_p (x) rho_Q) is the non-trivial-character part of the 4-fold cover's cohomology, and B1600's w21_check computes its Hodge-Riemann form blockwise (line 75, 'if p == q'), which is that typing's form.
